claim: On the SO-101 lift task, a policy pressed WITH per-episode visual randomization (headlight 0.5-1.5, front camera ±1 cm) vs WITHOUT, same 64 episodes, same dynamics DR, same trainer, judged on 80 matched trials under the SAME visual sweep at a pinned truth.

inputs.fixed.datasheet: 64 episodes, bases ['declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the conventional DR span)'], visual bases []
inputs.visual.datasheet: 64 episodes, bases ['declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the conventional DR span)'], visual bases ['declared visual span: headlight 0.5-1.5, front camera ±1 cm (the so101 scenes are lit by the headlight only, so the headlight scale is the visual span)']

caveats: The evaluation sweep equals the training sweep by design: this measures robustness inside the declared visual span, not generalization beyond it.
The scene's only light is MuJoCo's headlight; scene-light randomization is not exercised.
One camera (front, 576x1024): the three-camera rig trained 10x slower on the pod (1.4 step/s, 2026-09-04) and C1's earlier nulls were single-camera; comparability over coverage.
Artifacts repointed 2026-09-04 to tracked copies under docs/artifacts/lift-studies/ (rows, datasheets, study.json pulled from the volume before its prune).
